C901.text: Per-stratum results, coverage limits and the next improvement to fund

C902.text: The language identification model was trained for {F004} epochs on {F006} RMS training units ({F007} tokens). It passes all {F011} of {F012} checks: every language is at or above the {F016}% floor, and none has regressed below the base. Macro accuracy rose by {F013} points. The model is recorded as admitted.

C903.text: The result is strong but uneven in headroom. Kikamba ({F019}%) and Luhya ({F035}%) are closest to the floor, and Luhya abstains on {F038}% of items. The next improvement should therefore be targeted data for those two languages, followed by a review of abstention behaviour.

C904.text: The held-out results have been inspected, so they cannot count as independent final acceptance for any further recipe choice. This paper covers the retained measurements from this run only.

C905.text: All {F012} languages clear the accuracy floor; Kikamba and Luhya have the least headroom

C906.text: The language identification model was trained for {F004} epochs on {F006} RMS training units ({F007} tokens). It was scored on a sealed held-out set of {F008} units. It is recorded as admitted. Serving is a separate operation.

C907.text: All {F011} of {F012} checks pass and macro accuracy rose by {F013} points over the base. Kikamba ({F019}%) and Luhya ({F035}%) sit closest to the {F016}% floor. The held-out results have also now been inspected, so they cannot serve as independent final acceptance.

C908.text: Which model or dataset improvement should be funded next?

C909.text: Add Kikamba and Luhya data first, and review abstention for Luhya and Kiswahili. Commission fresh, sealed, independently labelled evaluation material before any further recipe selection. Each run took only {F009} GPU-hours, so single-change experiments are cheap.

C911.text: Every language clears its floor and none falls below the base

C912.text: {F011} of {F012} languages are at or above the {F016}% floor with no regression below the base. Macro accuracy rose by {F013} points.

C913.text: Gains are largest where the base was weakest: Kikamba rose from {F021}% to {F019}%, Ekegusii from {F017}% to {F015}%, and Luhya from {F037}% to {F035}%.

C914.text: Gikuyu ({F023}%, base {F025}%) and Kalenjin ({F027}%, base {F029}%) are comfortably clear. Kiswahili reaches {F039}% against a base of {F041}%, so little changed.

C915.text: Kikamba at {F019}% and Luhya at {F035}% have the thinnest margins over the floor, and Luhya abstains on {F038}% of items.

C916.text: All {F011} of {F012} languages are at or above the {F016}% floor and none falls below the base. The largest gains came where the base was weakest. Kikamba rose from {F021}% to {F019}%, Ekegusii from {F017}% to {F015}%, and Luhya from {F037}% to {F035}%. Gikuyu reached {F023}% from {F025}%, and Kalenjin {F027}% from {F029}%.

C917.text: Kiswahili is the exception in kind. Its base already scored {F041}%, and the model reaches {F039}%, so the gain there is small. Kikamba and Luhya have the thinnest margins over the floor, and a modest drop on fresh material could take either below it. That is the main reason to prioritise them.

C918.text: A modest, inexpensive run produced these results on a sealed evaluation set

C919.text: Training used {F006} units and {F007} tokens of RMS transcripts over {F004} epochs, spread across {F012} languages.

C920.text: The run took {F009} GPU-hours, or {F010} minutes on one GPU, so retraining is cheap in compute terms.

C921.text: Scoring used a sealed held-out set of {F008} units. The record gives no per-language split, so per-language uncertainty cannot be stated.

C922.text: Abstention runs from {F026}% for Gikuyu to {F042}% for Kiswahili. Luhya abstains on {F038}% of items and Kikamba on {F022}%.

C923.text: Training used {F006} units and {F007} tokens of RMS transcripts. Scoring used a sealed held-out set of {F008} units. The record does not split that set by language, so the uncertainty around each per-language figure cannot be stated. This matters most for Kikamba and Luhya, where margins are thin.

C924.text: The run took {F009} GPU-hours, or {F010} minutes on one GPU. Compute is therefore not the constraint on iteration. Abstention varies from {F026}% for Gikuyu to {F042}% for Kiswahili, with Luhya at {F038}% and Kikamba at {F022}%. The record does not say whether abstentions count as errors in the accuracy figures.

C925.text: Add Kikamba and Luhya data first, review abstention second, evaluate afresh before new recipes

C926.text: First, expand Kikamba and Luhya training and held-out data. They stand at {F019}% and {F035}% against a {F016}% floor and have the least headroom.

C927.text: Second, review abstention for Luhya ({F038}%) and Kiswahili ({F042}%). The record does not show whether abstentions count as errors, so confirm that before changing any threshold.

C928.text: Third, commission fresh, independently labelled sealed material before choosing another recipe, because the {F008} held-out units have now been inspected.

C929.text: Fourth, change one thing per run. At {F009} GPU-hours a run, any movement in Kikamba or Luhya can be attributed to a single change.

C930.text: First, expand Kikamba and Luhya training and held-out data, since these have the least headroom over the {F016}% floor. Second, confirm how abstention is scored, then review it for Luhya ({F038}%) and Kiswahili ({F042}%). Changing a threshold before knowing this could move accuracy without improving the model.

C931.text: Third, commission fresh, independently labelled sealed material before selecting another recipe, because the {F008} held-out units have been inspected. Fourth, change one thing per run. At {F009} GPU-hours a run, this is affordable and lets any change in Kikamba or Luhya be attributed to its cause.

C932.text: The record supports the stated checks only, not independent acceptance or wider performance

C933.text: Performance outside these {F012} languages and the sealed set is not established. An independently designed evaluation would close this gap.

C934.text: Final acceptance cannot be called independent after further recipe selection, because these results have been inspected. Fresh, independently labelled, sealed material would close it.

C935.text: Lineage from objective to production is incomplete: no new production plan is linked to this historical run. Only an explicitly compiled, evidence-linked objective closes it.

C936.text: Serving is separate: the full adapter is served, the pruned adapter is admitted but not served. Privacy handling of the transcripts is not evidenced in this record.

C937.text: Performance outside the measured languages and the sealed set is not established; an independently designed evaluation would close that gap. Independent final acceptance is not possible after further recipe selection on inspected results, and needs fresh, sealed, independently labelled material.

C938.text: No new production plan is linked to this historical run, so lineage from objective to production is incomplete. Closing it needs an explicitly compiled, evidence-linked objective, never a backdated assumption. Serving is a separate operation: the full adapter is served and the pruned adapter is admitted but not served. The record carries no evidence on privacy handling of the transcripts.
